data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'kh-th-r', meaning to 'remind' or 'admonish'. In Islamic context, it refers to the Angel Khidr who guides and reminds Prophet Moses of Allah's will. The name Khathir carries the meaning “Reminder, Warning” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khathir usually hope their child will grow to embody reminder, warning and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: خَثِير
in_arabic.meaning: مُبارَك و مُبارَكَة وَ مُبَارَكٌ وَ هُوَ الَّذي يَبارَكُ فِي الَخَلقِ
in_arabic.long_meaning: نَسبَت لِأَحَدِ الصِفَاتِ الَّتي فَضَلَت عَن مُحَمَدٍ صَلَى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ سَلَم، وَ هِيَ الصِفَةُ الَّتي يَقُولُ اللَهُ تَعَالَى: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَثِيرَةٌ بِالْبُيُوتِ وَالَّذِي يُرِيدُ الْفَخَرَ الَّذِي لَا يَنَالُهُ) سورة غافر: 8، وَ كَذَلِكَ فُضَلَ عَلَيْهِ الَّذي يُقَولُ: خَثِيرٌ، وَ هِيَ مِنْ قَولِ اللَهِ تَعَالَى: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ خَثِيرَةٌ بِالْبُيُوتِ) سورة ق: 8، وَ هَذِهِ الصِفَةُ مِنَ الصِفَاتِ الَّتي تُعطى لِأَبي مُحَمَدٍ وَ هِيَ الصِفَةُ الَّتي يَقُولُ اللَهُ تَعَالَى: (وَقُلِ ادْعُ مَنِ اِستَطَعْتَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَهِ يَمِينًا لِتَقَوَّمَ مَنِ اِستَطَعْتَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَهِ ثُمَ يَقَوَّمُ بِكَ مُضَرُ وَ يَخَثِيرُ) سورة إبراهيم: 21، وَ هَذِهِ الصِفَةُ مِنَ الصِفَاتِ الَّتي تُعطى لِجَدّي مُحَمَدٍ وَ هِيَ الصِفَةُ الَّتي يَقُولُ اللَهُ تَعَالَى: (وَمَضَرُ وَ يَخَثِيرُ بِاِسمِ الَّذي يَقُولُ: يَخَثِيرُ) سورة إبراهيم: 21، وَ كَذَلِكَ فُضَلَ عَلَيْهِ الَّذي يُقَولُ: خَثِيرَةُ، وَ هِيَ مِنْ قَولِ اللَهِ تَعَالَى: (وَمَضَرُ وَ يَخَثِيرُ بِاِسمِ الَّذي يَقُولُ: يَخَثِيرُ) سورة إبراهيم: 21، وَ هَذِهِ الصِفَةُ مِنَ الصِفَاتِ الَّتي تُعطى لِأَبي مُحَمَدٍ وَ هِيَ الصِفَةُ الَّتي يَقُولُ اللَهُ تَعَالَى: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَثِيرَةٌ بِالْبُيُوتِ وَالَّذِي يُرِيدُ الْفَخَرَ الَّذِي لَا يَنَالُهُ) سورة غافر: 8، وَ كَذَلِكَ فُضَلَ عَلَيْهِ الَّذي يُقَولُ: خَثِيرَةٌ، وَ هِيَ مِنْ قَولِ اللَهِ تَعَالَى: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ خَثِيرَةٌ بِالْبُيُوتِ) سورة ق: 8

in_english.name: Khathir
in_english.meaning: Blessed and blessed one, who is blessed in creation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Khathir is derived from the Arabic root 'kh-th-r', which means 'blessed' or 'blessed one'. In Islamic tradition, the blessed one refers to a person who is favored by Allah and has been granted spiritual blessings. The name Khathir is also associated with the Quranic verse, "And He is the one who sends blessings down upon the houses (of the righteous)" (Quran 40:8). In this context, the blessed one is one who has been blessed with spiritual blessings and has been granted a high status in the eyes of Allah. The name Khathir is also used to refer to a person who is blessed with good fortune and prosperity. In Islamic tradition, the blessed one is considered to be one who is close to Allah and has been granted spiritual blessings. The name Khathir is also associated with the concept of barakah, which refers to the blessings and favors that Allah grants to His servants. In this sense, the blessed one is one who has been granted spiritual blessings and has been favored by Allah.

It is the name of an important character in Islamic folklore – Angel Khidr, also known as Al-Khadir or Khadir Al-Abtallah (the Green one). He is believed to be a gifted sage from the ancient nations, who acted as a guide and teacher for Prophet Moses (PBUH) during his voyages.

The name Khathir is also mentioned in relation to a prominent Sufi scholar named Abdul Qadir Jilani. He is believed to have been born in the town of Shahjahanpur, near the city of Baghdad, in 1077 CE, and died there in 1166 CE. The name Khathir is used to describe the spiritual and transformative journey of a Sufi, which is characterized by detachment from worldly concerns and the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and enlightenment.
